rows.jp: 夜が暑苦しくないのが、田舎のいいとこだ。
rows.en: One good thing about the countryside was that the nights never got stifling.

ghs.en: One good thing of countryside is that the evenings are not sticky damp hot.
ghs.assessment: The source calls it a virtue of the countryside that nights are not oppressively hot. 'One good thing of countryside' lacks an article, while 'sticky damp' adds specific humidity imagery.
ghs.remedy: Use 'One good thing about the countryside is that the nights aren't oppressively hot.'

highlights.text: One good thing of countryside is that the evenings are not sticky damp hot.

rows.jp: 窓から滑り込む風はほどよく冷たく、肌に優しい。
rows.en: The breeze slipping in through the window was pleasantly cool, gentle against my skin.

ghs.en: The wind that slips through the window is cold with moderation, and gentle on the skin.
ghs.assessment: ほどよく冷たい means pleasantly or comfortably cool. 'Cold with moderation' is a literal and unnatural collocation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The breeze slipping through the window is pleasantly cool and gentle on my skin.'

highlights.text: The wind that slips through the window is cold with moderation, and gentle on the skin.

ghs.assessment: My stomach's empty is ordinary English metonymy for hunger, so the wrong-subject claim is false. The confirmed defect is the non-US innit register.
ghs.remedy: Use a natural US-English hunger line.

highlights.text: Taichi: "...stomach's empty, innit..."

rows.jp: 独り言なども適度にこなしつつ、日記を書き綴る。
rows.en: Having filled my quota of talking to myself, I went on writing in my diary.

ghs.en: While digesting a suitable soliloquy, I keep chronicle in the diary.
ghs.assessment: The narrator writes continuously in his diary while working in a suitable amount of talking to himself. 'Digesting a suitable soliloquy' substitutes a food metaphor, and 'keep chronicle in the diary' is not grammatical English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I continue writing in my diary, indulging in a suitable amount of soliloquy as I go.'

highlights.text: While digesting a suitable soliloquy, I keep chronicle in the diary.

rows.jp: がるるるるるるるるる
腹の虫がうごうご咆吼を繰り返す。
rows.en: The beast in my belly writhed and roared again.

ghs.en: The belly bug steadily repeats its rice, bowl growl.

rows.jp: さながら自らを囲う身の程弁えない檻に対して敵意を剥く獅子の如く。
rows.en: Like a lion baring its fangs at the presumptuous cage that dared contain it.

ghs.en: As if a lion, baring animosity against the cage that surrounds it, unaware of what it imprisons.
ghs.assessment: 身の程弁えない modifies the cage. GHS keeps the quality on the cage but weakens presumptuousness into ignorance of what it imprisons.
ghs.remedy: Describe the presumptuous cage containing the lion.

highlights.text: As if a lion, baring animosity against the cage that surrounds it, unaware of what it imprisons.

rows.jp: 『食えよ、テメエ食えよっ！　食うぞ！』
rows.en: “Eat, asshole! Eat! Or I’ll eat you!”

ghs.en: Belly Bug: 『Eat! Eat now ya prick! Devour!』
ghs.assessment: The source may omit the object, but GHS shifts I'll eat you into an imperative Devour. Preserve the speaker and threat relation.
ghs.remedy: Use an elliptical first-person threat.

highlights.text: Belly Bug: 『Eat! Eat now ya prick! Devour!』

rows.jp: 「うるさいな。なんだそれ、ギャグか」
rows.en: “Shut up. What was that supposed to be, a joke?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Shaddap. What's even this, some sketch?"
ghs.assessment: Sketch is a recognizable type of comedy bit but is narrower and British-coded compared with ギャグ.
ghs.remedy: Use bit, gag, or joke in US English.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Shaddap. What's even this, some sketch?"

rows.jp: 『腹減ってんだよ！　食えって！　俺だけの問題じゃねぇんだぞ！』
rows.en: “I’m starving! Feed me! This isn’t just my problem, you know!”

ghs.en: Belly Bug: 『Yer tummy's empty! Chow something! This ain't just my problem yannow!』
ghs.assessment: The personified belly saying your tummy's empty still establishes shared hunger and enables the next line. The issue is voice and personification, not a critical subject reversal.
ghs.remedy: Keep the belly's voice without changing the addressee relation.

highlights.text: Belly Bug: 『Yer tummy's empty! Chow something! This ain't just my problem yannow!』

rows.jp: 「短気なやつだ。萩原朔太郎の詩に出てくるタコみたいに自分の脚でも食ってろよ。全部食いきったら永遠の存在になれるぞ」
rows.en: “Short fuse on you. Go eat your own legs like the octopus in Sakutarō Hagiwara’s poem. Once you finish them all, you can live forever.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Short tempered aren't we! Maybe I should do like that octopus in the Sakutarou Hagiwara poem and start eating my own legs. If I manage to eat myself completely without leaving anything behind, then I'll have achieved eternal life!"
ghs.assessment: The narrator tells the belly-creature to eat its own legs like the octopus in Hagiwara Sakutarō's poem. 'Maybe I should ... eat my own legs' makes the narrator perform it. The poet's name is also given in non-Hepburn order and spelling.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Eat your own legs like the octopus in Hagiwara Sakutarō's poem. Once you've eaten every last bit, you can become eternal.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Short tempered aren't we! Maybe I should do like that octopus in the Sakutarou Hagiwara poem and start eating my own legs. If I manage to eat myself completely without leaving anything behind, then I'll have achieved eternal life!"

rows.jp: 『馬鹿にしやがって！　舐めてんのか！』
rows.en: “You making fun of me?! You think I’m a joke?!”

ghs.en: Belly bug: 『That's nonsense that is! Ya pulling my leg now!』
ghs.assessment: Pulling my leg imperfectly narrows the accusation but retains mockery or deception. Major severity overstates the shift.
ghs.remedy: Use don't mess with me or equivalent.

highlights.text: Belly bug: 『That's nonsense that is! Ya pulling my leg now!』

ghs.en: Taichi: "Whatcha gonna do if I am? Eh?"
Taichi: "Go ahead and try, you figment of my imagination!"

rows.jp: 『みくびるなよ！　俺はスゥィートに育てられた芸能人の息子ばりに無軌道なんだぜ？』
rows.en: “Don’t underestimate me! I’m as out of control as a celebrity brat raised in a penthouse suite!”

ghs.en: Belly bug: 『Don't be belittlin' me! I'm as rambunctious as the son of some entertainer brought up all sweet yannow!』

rows.jp: 「フー、そいつはクールだ。けどおまえのスウィートガイっぷりも、肉体という檻の中じゃ実刑判決で豚箱入りした芸能人の息子ばりに無力だってことを忘れるな」
rows.en: “Whew. Very cool. All that suite life may have made you one sweet guy, but inside this prison of flesh, you’re as helpless as a celebrity’s son doing hard time.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ohhh, we got a wise guy here. Well, while you're in the gaol known as the flesh, don'tcha forget that even with your Sweet Guy manners you are as powerless as the son of an entertainer that was slammed in the pigpen to serve his just sentence!"
ghs.assessment: Wise guy changes that's cool, but the broader comic mechanism survives.
ghs.remedy: Preserve the approving cool judgment.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ohhh, we got a wise guy here. Well, while you're in the gaol known as the flesh, don'tcha forget that even with your Sweet Guy manners you are as powerless as the son of an entertainer that was slammed in the pigpen to serve his just sentence!"

rows.en: “Why, you—I’ve let you run your mouth long enough!”

ghs.en: Belly bug: 『How dare you! You had to go and say it!』

rows.jp: と、俺くらいの人間ともなると、こうして観念的な存在とも意思の疎通がはかれるのである。
rows.en: A man of my caliber could communicate even with a purely conceptual being.

ghs.en: And with the presence of this two-way communication with an existence most assuredly conceptual, there lies the measure of how much of a human I am.
ghs.assessment: The boast says that a person on the narrator's level can communicate even with a conceptual entity. The English makes the communication a measure of 'how much of a human' he is, changing ability into humanity.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Once you're as much of a man as I am, you can even communicate with conceptual entities like this.'

highlights.text: And with the presence of this two-way communication with an existence most assuredly conceptual, there lies the measure of how much of a human I am.

rows.jp: そういうの一般的にキチ○イって言いますかそうですか。
rows.en: And apparently society calls that being a l○natic. I see.

ghs.en: Is that what they generally call lu**cy perhaps indeed that is so.
ghs.assessment: Lu**cy transparently preserves censorship of lunacy. The confirmed defect is malformed grammar, not an unrecoverable target.
ghs.remedy: Keep the censorship and repair the sentence.

highlights.text: Is that what they generally call lu**cy perhaps indeed that is so.

rows.jp: 「しかし本当にハラは減った、と」

rows.en: I should find something to eat.

ghs.assessment: 階下に is a direction fragment equivalent to 'Downstairs.' 'To downstairs' is not grammatical English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Downstairs.'

highlights.text: To downstairs.

rows.jp: 冷蔵庫の中身はからっぽになっていた。

ghs.en: The contents of the refrigerator had become void.

rows.jp: 電気も通ってないから、何も保存できないしな。
rows.en: With no electricity, I couldn’t keep anything fresh anyway.

ghs.en: Without electricity, the preservation of anything is impossible.

ghs.assessment: 戸棚類をあさる means rummaging through the cupboards or cabinets. 'Rustle in the cupboard' names a sound or slight movement and incorrectly narrows the plural storage furniture.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I rummage through the cupboards.'

highlights.text: I rustle in the cupboard.

rows.jp: ……これはまったくもって完膚無きまでに何の役にも立たないので捨てる。
rows.en: ...They were, in every conceivable respect, completely useless. I threw them out.

ghs.en: ...those I completely and entirely cast aside for being absolutely, completely and thoroughly useless.
There was a pepperful of exaggeration.
ghs.assessment: Pepperful of exaggeration retains pepper but adds an opaque pun. It is intrusive wordplay, not a critical semantic collapse.
ghs.remedy: Keep the pepper exaggeration without an opaque coinage.

highlights.text: There was a pepperful of exaggeration.

rows.jp: ジャガイモもあったぞ。

ghs.en: There was some Solanum Tuberosum (potatoes), too!

rows.jp: 机の上に、それらを並べる。
rows.en: I arranged everything on the table.

ghs.en: I line them up over the table.
ghs.assessment: Over versus on the table is a small prepositional error.
ghs.remedy: Use on the table.

highlights.text: I line them up over the table.

rows.jp: 剃毛する時にも似た音を立て、塩ふり生ジャガイモを齧る。
rows.en: Making a sound not unlike someone shaving, I gnawed on the salted raw potato.

ghs.en: Unable to resist the appeeling sound of the act, I add salt on a potato I had a-peeled and took a bite.

rows.jp: 「ほー、これが新ジャガの風味かぁ、んがぐぐ……適度に固くて、まるで石のよう……」
rows.en: “Ohhh, so this is what a new potato tastes like. Nghgh... nice and firm. Like a rock...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, this is the taste of a tiny little New Potato then, mnghmngh... so moderately adamantine, almost at the levels of a rock..."
ghs.assessment: Japanese number is neutral here. Retain only the genuine degree or idiom problem, not an English-number allegation.
ghs.remedy: Use natural English without unsupported degree.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ahhh, this is the taste of a tiny little New Potato then, mnghmngh... so moderately adamantine, almost at the levels of a rock..."

rows.jp: 「って、食えるかこんなモン！　なめんな！」
rows.en: “How the hell am I supposed to eat this?! Don’t fuck with me!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Wait, is this crap even edible?! Don't be pulling my leg!"
ghs.assessment: Don't be pulling my leg imperfectly localizes don't mock or mess with me while addressing the belly. The core accusation survives.
ghs.remedy: Use don't mess with me.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Wait, is this crap even edible?! Don't be pulling my leg!"

ghs.assessment: The Japanese noun is number-neutral, so number alone cannot sustain the finding. The remaining issue is idiom.
ghs.remedy: Render the noun naturally without forcing number.

highlights.text: I tossed it.

rows.jp: 「ペッペッ、芽まで囓っちまった！　毒なのに！（本当）」
rows.en: “Ptooey! I even bit the sprout! It’s poisonous! (True.)”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Pah! pah! I gnawed it to the bud! This stuff's poisonous! (Seriously.)"
ghs.assessment: 芽 is the potato sprout or eye, not a flower bud. He says he bit even that toxic part; 'gnawed it to the bud' instead describes reaching a destination.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Ptooey! I even bit into a sprout—and those are poisonous! (True.)'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Pah! pah! I gnawed it to the bud! This stuff's poisonous! (Seriously.)"

rows.jp: そして俺は気づくのだった。
rows.en: That was when it dawned on me.

ghs.en: And that was when I realized,

ghs.assessment: Terror ensues overstates the affect but preserves the shock beat.
ghs.remedy: Use a less inflated startled reaction.

highlights.text: Terror ensues.

rows.jp: 「そうか、パンがなければケーキを食べればいい……ププ！」
rows.en: “Of course. If they have no bread, let them eat cake... Pfft!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Right! If we have no bread, then let us eat cake... pffft!"

rows.jp: 餓えた民衆が聞いたら抱腹絶倒間違いなしのナイスギャグだ。
rows.en: The starving masses would split their sides at that absolute killer.

ghs.en: A nice gag that will fill the bellies of the starving populace with laughter, no mistake.

rows.jp: そのくらいの度量が民にもいるってことだね。
rows.en: They could stand to learn how to take a joke.

ghs.en: That's how much magnanimity people have, don't they.
ghs.assessment: The source says the people need that much generosity or tolerance. 'That's how much magnanimity people have' changes necessity into a claim about what they already possess.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The people need at least that much generosity of spirit.'

highlights.text: That's how much magnanimity people have, don't they.

rows.jp: 「ということでピザを取ろう」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, if it's gotta be like this, I'll just order a pizza."

ghs.assessment: Picking up the phone is a natural first-step metonym for calling. It only leaves the completed call implicit.
ghs.remedy: State the call if completion matters.

highlights.text: I pick up the telephone.

rows.jp: 「すいません黒須ですけどダブチスペＭ一枚……」%N※ダブチスペ＝現実語。ダブルチーズスペシャルの略。本当にこう呼ばれている。
rows.en: “Hi, this is Kurosu. One medium Dub-Chee-Spec...”%N*The Japanese uses dabuchispe, an actual abbreviation of Double Cheese Special.

rows.jp: 「あー、まだ制覇してないメニューがあったのにー！！」
rows.en: “And I hadn’t even conquered the whole menu yet!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, but I still hadn't finished conquering all their offeriiings!!!"
The life of a human is filled with regrets.

rows.jp: 「そうか、じゃがいもがあるんだった」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well then, I only got potatoes."
ghs.assessment: Japanese number is neutral; keep only genuine added degree or idiom issues.
ghs.remedy: Avoid unsupported degree while choosing natural number.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Well then, I only got potatoes."

rows.en: All I had to do was steam them.
I went out to the yard.

rows.jp: サバイバルマンガを参考にして炊飯の用意をする。
rows.en: Using a survival manga as my guide, I prepared to cook.

ghs.en: Using a survival manga as reference, I set up a cooking fire.

rows.jp: 蒸すのは面倒なので、焼くことにする。
rows.en: Steaming them sounded like a pain, so I decided to roast them.

ghs.en: Steaming is too much of a mess, so I settled for roasting.

rows.jp: ここで簡単なじゃがバターの作り方をば。
rows.en: And now, a simple recipe for buttered potatoes.

ghs.en: Here we are, a simple recipe for buttered potatoes:

rows.jp: ジャガイモに一人一人名前をつける。
rows.en: Name each potato, one by one.

ghs.en: Baptize the potatoes one by one.

rows.jp: ホイルに包んだジャガイモを断腸の思いで石に放り込む（風味が増す）。
rows.en: With a gut-wrenching sense of loss, throw the foil-wrapped potatoes onto the stones. (Adds flavor.)

ghs.en:
Toss the tinfoil into which the potatoes are
wrapped onto the stones while reminiscing of
your broken heart (improves the taste).
ghs.assessment: 断腸の思いで means throwing them in with heart-rending reluctance. 'While reminiscing of your broken heart' changes immediate emotion into second-person recollection and is not idiomatic English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'With a heavy heart, throw the foil-wrapped potatoes onto the stones. (Improves the flavor.)'

highlights.text:
Toss the tinfoil into which the potatoes are
wrapped onto the stones while reminiscing of
your broken heart (improves the taste).

rows.jp: 哀しみを乗り越えて人として大きくなる。
rows.en: Rise above your grief and grow as a person.

ghs.en: Surmount the grief to become a stronger person.

rows.en: Silence the beast in your belly.

rows.jp: 取り出して皿にうつす。
rows.en: Remove the potatoes and transfer them to a plate.

rows.jp: バター……はないので塩をかける。
rows.en: Add butter... except there isn’t any, so add salt.

ghs.en: Add butter... that I don't have so salt instead.

rows.jp: じゃがバターじゃないじゃん？とかいう些細な疑問を払拭する。
rows.en: Dismiss the petty objection that these aren’t buttered potatoes.

ghs.en:
Sweep away trivial questions like, "well how're
they buttered potatoes then?"

ghs.assessment: Devour completes the linked faux-archaic recipe cadence, but is stronger than formal 食す.
ghs.remedy: Keep the mock formality with a less forceful eat verb.

highlights.text: Devour.

ghs.assessment: The proposition survives; the defect is grammar rather than major semantic change.
ghs.remedy: Repair the sentence.

highlights.text: Alive aren't I, me.

rows.jp: 玄関先で人が倒れるのが見えた。
rows.en: I saw someone collapse outside the front door.

ghs.en: At the front door I could see a person collapsing.

rows.jp: 桐原冬子その人だった。
rows.en: It was none other than Touko Kirihara.

ghs.en: The person in question was Kirihara Touko.

rows.jp: 俺はじゃがいもを貪り食いながら、冬子を見下ろした。
rows.en: I looked down at Touko as I wolfed down a potato.

ghs.en: While greedily devouring a potato, I look down on Touko.

rows.jp: 俺は二個目のじゃがいもを貪りだした。
rows.en: I began wolfing down a second potato.

ghs.en: I began devouring a second potato.

rows.jp: 俺は三個目のじゃがいもを―――
rows.en: I reached for my third potato—

ghs.en: Touko: "Hurry up and help me already..."

ghs.assessment: The source gives a complete observation that she appears to be suffering. 'Appears in pain' omits the subject and leaves an English fragment.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She looks as though she is in pain.'

highlights.text: Appears in pain.

ghs.assessment: どうした asks what is wrong with the person. 'What're you here for?' instead asks her purpose in coming and omits concern for her condition.
ghs.remedy: Use 'What's wrong?'

highlights.text: Touko: "What're you here for?"

rows.jp: 「ふむ。その匂いをたどってここまで？」
rows.en: “Hm. And followed it all the way here?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Hoh. You followed said smell to here then?"
ghs.assessment: The path and action survive through legalistic register and an awkward idiom.
ghs.remedy: Use natural wording for the path.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Hoh. You followed said smell to here then?"

ghs.en: She no longer is capable of a response.
ghs.assessment: Incapacity overstates a stopped response, but contextual nonresponsiveness is real. This is aspect, not event replacement.
ghs.remedy: Describe the response stopping.

highlights.text: She no longer is capable of a response.

rows.jp: 俺は三つ目のじゃがいもを食べ終わってから、冬子の体を引き起こした。
rows.en: After finishing my third potato, I pulled Touko upright.

ghs.en: Once I finished eating my third potato, I dragged Touko's body over.
ghs.assessment: The narrator pulls Tōko's body upright after finishing the potato. 'Dragged ... over' changes the direction to horizontal relocation and makes the action sound like moving a corpse.
ghs.remedy: Use 'After finishing my third potato, I pull Tōko upright.'

highlights.text: Once I finished eating my third potato, I dragged Touko's body over.

rows.jp: 冬子がじゃがいもを貪り食う。

ghs.assessment: じゃがいも is number-neutral. The confirmed defect is the unsupported superlative, not plural potatoes.
ghs.remedy: Remove the superlative.

highlights.text: Touko most greedily devours potatoes.

rows.jp: 咀嚼してない時間があってはならないとばかりに。
rows.en: As if even a single second without chewing were forbidden.

ghs.en: Because she didn't seem to have even the time to chew.
ghs.assessment: The source says she eats as if she cannot allow even a moment when she is not chewing. 'Because she didn't seem to have even the time to chew' says the opposite: that she lacks time for chewing.
ghs.remedy: Use 'As though she could not permit a single moment without chewing.'

highlights.text: Because she didn't seem to have even the time to chew.

rows.jp: 猛然と、勇猛果敢に、徹底して、食べる。

ghs.en: A savage, dauntlessly courageous, thorough eating.
ghs.assessment: The source piles adverbs onto the woman's act of eating. 'A savage, dauntlessly courageous, thorough eating' turns the action into an ungrammatical abstract noun phrase and removes the eater.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She eats ferociously, fearlessly, relentlessly.'

highlights.text: A savage, dauntlessly courageous, thorough eating.

rows.jp: 思い返せば、人前で食すことを恥じらっていた冬子だ。
rows.en: Come to think of it, Touko had always been embarrassed to eat in front of other people.

ghs.en: In retrospect, Touko was always embarrassed about eating in front of others.
This thing now is a rarity.
ghs.assessment: The source meaning survives through grammar and idiom problems.
ghs.remedy: Render the line naturally.

highlights.text: This thing now is a rarity.

rows.en: “...What have you been muttering this whole time?”

ghs.en: Touko: "...what's that you keep talking about now?"
ghs.assessment: The core action survives; only grammar and idiom are defective.
ghs.remedy: Repair the English execution.

highlights.text: Touko: "...what's that you keep talking about now?"

rows.jp: 「おまえの血肉になった新じゃがの無辜(むこ)なる民たちだ」
rows.en: “The innocent citizens of New Potato who have become your flesh and blood.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The blameless, innocent people of the New Potato Republic that have now become your flesh and blood."

rows.jp: じゃがいものかけらを頬につけて、冬子は怪訝な顔をした。

ghs.en: With bits of potato stuck to her cheek, Touko made a puzzled face.
ghs.assessment: The civic potato metaphor is already source-supported. Only redundant wording remains.
ghs.remedy: Remove the redundant blameless, innocent pairing.

highlights.text: With bits of potato stuck to her cheek, Touko made a puzzled face.

ghs.en: Taichi: "Don't worry about it, it's fine."

rows.jp: 「命は受け継がれていくのだ」
rows.en: “Their lives will live on in you.”
I pressed my palms together in prayer.

rows.jp: しばらくきょとんとした顔をしていた。
rows.en: She stared at me blankly for a while.

ghs.en: She showed a somewhat stumped face,

rows.en: I handed her a plastic bottle.

ghs.remedy: Use natural English.

highlights.text: Touko: "MnchMnch."

rows.jp: 大人びて見えるけど、年相応に子供なんだよな、こいつ……。
rows.en: For all her mature looks, she was still as much a kid as anyone else her age...

ghs.en: She looks all grown up, but she has the mannerism of a child, this one...
ghs.assessment: The proposition survives; the confirmed issue is grammar and phrasing.
ghs.remedy: Repair the English execution.

highlights.text: She looks all grown up, but she has the mannerism of a child, this one...

rows.jp: 七個か八個もたいらげて、ようやく冬子は一息ついた。
rows.en: After polishing off seven or eight potatoes, Touko finally paused for breath.

ghs.en: After having flattened seven or eight, finally Touko takes a breather.
ghs.assessment: たいらげる means to polish off or finish eating food. 'Flattened seven or eight' literalizes the verb into a physical action on the potatoes.
ghs.remedy: Use 'After polishing off seven or eight, Tōko finally pauses for breath.'

highlights.text: After having flattened seven or eight, finally Touko takes a breather.

rows.jp: 冬子は居住まいを正した。
俯いて、上目づかいに俺を見る。
rows.en: With her head bowed, she peered up at me.

ghs.en: With her head hung in shame, she rolls up her eyes to look at me.
ghs.assessment: 上目づかい means looking upward from beneath lowered brows, not rolling the eyes. 'In shame' also supplies an emotion not explicitly stated by 俯いて.
ghs.remedy: Use 'With her head lowered, she looks up at me through her lashes.'

highlights.text: With her head hung in shame, she rolls up her eyes to look at me.

rows.jp: だもんで、俺も冬子を見る。
rows.en: So I looked back at her.

ghs.en: And so I, too, look at Touko.

ghs.assessment: じっと見る is a complete present action. 'Staring fixed' is an unattached participle with a nonstandard adjective where an adverb is required.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I stare.'

highlights.text: Staring fixed.

ghs.en: She looks down, her face red.

rows.jp: ちょっとドキドキしてしまった。
rows.en: My heart gave a little flutter.

ghs.en: It made my heart go a bit boom-boom.

rows.jp: 「い、いやなに。そっちがメンチを切るからつい」
rows.en: “I-it’s nothing. You were staring me down first.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "N-,no I wasn't! I only glanced that way unconsciously!"
ghs.assessment: メンチを切る is to glare at or stare someone down. 'I only glanced that way unconsciously' changes the other person's deliberate stare into the narrator's accidental glance and removes the idiom's force.
ghs.remedy: Use 'N-no, it was only because you were glaring at me.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "N-,no I wasn't! I only glanced that way unconsciously!"

ghs.en: Touko: "I'm trying to say something polite here!"
ghs.assessment: The speaker says she was trying to thank him. 'Trying to say something polite' weakens the specific act of gratitude and shifts the tense to the present.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I was trying to thank you!'

highlights.text: Touko: "I'm trying to say something polite here!"

ghs.assessment: ぎこちなかった is a complete past judgment that the attempt was awkward. 'So very awkwardly' is an adverb fragment with no verb or subject.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It was awkward.'

highlights.text: So very awkwardly.

rows.jp: 「まさか餓えていたとは思わなかった」
rows.en: “I never would’ve guessed you were literally starving.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I couldn't even imagine you were flat-out starving."

rows.jp: 冬子はさらに赤面した。

ghs.en: Touko's face grew even more red.

rows.jp: 「家に食料なかったとですか？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Was it because there was no food in the house?"
ghs.assessment: The mock-dialect question asks whether there was no food at her house. 'Was it because' invents a causal frame and removes the dialectal comic coloration.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Weren't there no food at home?' or another controlled comic dialect form.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Was it because there was no food in the house?"

rows.jp: 「どう調理していいかわからなくて」
rows.en: “I didn’t know how to cook any of it.”

ghs.en: Touko: "I don't really know how to prepare it."
ghs.assessment: She explains that she did not know how to prepare the food she had. The English present tense makes it a standing inability rather than the cause of the completed starvation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I didn't know how to cook it.'

highlights.text: Touko: "I don't really know how to prepare it."

rows.en: “But didn’t you say you were a good cook...?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But, but, that time, you said you were a great cook..."

rows.jp: 「あれ、だって昔弁当とか作って……」
rows.en: “But you used to make those lunches...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Then, those bentos you had weren't made..."
ghs.assessment: The interrupted question recalls the lunches she used to make. 'The bentos you had weren't made' changes her role from maker to possessor and prematurely supplies a negative passive continuation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'But what about the lunches you used to make...?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Then, those bentos you had weren't made..."

rows.jp: 「お手伝いさんが作ったのを私が作ったってことにして」
rows.en: “Our housekeeper made them. I just pretended I had.”

ghs.en: Touko: "The maid made them and I just made it look like I made them."
ghs.assessment: The helper made the lunches and Tōko passed them off as her own. 'Made it look like I made them' mismatches singular and plural objects and weakens the deliberate attribution.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The maid made them, and I pretended I had.'

highlights.text: Touko: "The maid made them and I just made it look like I made them."

rows.jp: 「お手伝いさんって……何歳くらいの？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "The maid... how old is she?"

rows.jp: 「……おばちゃん弁当に……俺は……ときめいて……」
rows.en: “I got butterflies... over some middle-aged lady’s lunchboxes...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...my heart fluttered... for the bento... prepared by an old bag..."
ghs.assessment: おばちゃん is a familiar, mildly disparaging middle-aged lady or auntie. 'Old bag' adds a much harsher contemptuous insult not supported by the line.
ghs.remedy: Use 'My heart fluttered over a middle-aged lady's lunch...'

highlights.text: Taichi: "...my heart fluttered... for the bento... prepared by an old bag..."

rows.jp: 「じゃ自宅に戻れば肉なり缶詰なりあるわけだ」
rows.en: “So if you go home, there’ll be meat, canned goods, whatever.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "So, if you go back home, I guess there should be some meat, or some canned food."

ghs.assessment: The source writes the English loanword 'really' in katakana for the reaction. 'MAJIII' substitutes a different Japanese slang word and leaves it as untranslated romanization.
ghs.remedy: Use 'REALLY?!' while preserving the marked comic delivery.

highlights.text: Taichi: "MAJIII!?"

rows.jp: 缶詰の存在を知らないっ？
rows.en: She didn’t know canned goods existed?

ghs.en: She doesn't even know of the existence of canned food!?"
ghs.assessment: The English thought ends with an unmatched quotation mark after the exclamation and question marks.
ghs.remedy: Remove the stray closing quotation mark.

highlights.text: She doesn't even know of the existence of canned food!?"

rows.jp: 缶詰という単語を知らない？
rows.en: She didn’t even know the phrase?

ghs.en: She doesn't know the words 'canned food'?

rows.jp: エンサイクロペディア冬子には缶詰の二文字がない？
rows.en: The Touko Encyclopedia had no entry under CANNED GOODS?

ghs.en: Do those two words never appear together in the Encyclopedia Touka?
ghs.assessment: Touka has the wrong final vowel. The project spelling is ASCII Touko; no macron is required.
ghs.remedy: Use Touko.

highlights.text: Do those two words never appear together in the Encyclopedia Touka?

rows.jp: え？　いやそりゃ金持ちだって知ってたけど……え、本気ですか？
rows.en: I mean, sure, I knew she was rich, but... seriously?

ghs.en: Eh? No, I know that she's rich, but still... ehhh, seriously?

rows.jp: 「キャビアって缶詰に入ってるんじゃないの？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Doesn't your caviar come in a can?!"

rows.jp: わなわな震えながら問う。

ghs.en: A question while I shake and tremble with fear.
ghs.assessment: The source says the narrator asks while trembling with agitation. 'A question while I shake and tremble with fear' is a noun fragment, redundantly doubles the motion, and adds fear as its cause.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I ask, trembling.'

highlights.text: A question while I shake and tremble with fear.

rows.jp: 「ビンよ。毎週木箱に詰められて外国から送られてくるの」
rows.en: “It comes in jars. Every week, a wooden crate arrives from overseas.”

ghs.en: Touko: "It's in jars. Every week, jam-packed in a wooden box sent from overseas."

rows.jp: 平常的に食ってるッッッ！？
rows.en: SHE ATE CAVIAR ON A REGULAR BASIS?!

rows.jp: 「ケーキがなかったらキャビアとパンで食いつなげよ金持ち野郎！」
rows.en: “If there’s no cake, live on caviar and bread, you rich bastard!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If you have no cake, then live on bread and caviar, you damn upper class twit!"

rows.jp: 「ど、どうして怒るの？　それにケーキって……？？？」
rows.en: “W-why are you angry? And what cake...?”

ghs.en: Touko: "Wh-, what are you angry for? And what's this about cake...???"

rows.jp: 「キャビー！　こんなありがたみのわからない女に食われて！　おうおう！」
rows.en: “Cavi! To think you’d be eaten by a woman who never appreciated you! Oh, Cavi, Cavi!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "CAVIEEE! Eaten by this woman of all values ignorant! All the time!"
ghs.assessment: ありがたみのわからない女 is a woman who does not appreciate the caviar's value. 'Woman of all values ignorant' is not grammatical, while おうおう is mock weeping rather than 'all the time.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'Cavvy! Eaten by a woman who doesn't appreciate you! Boo-hoo!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "CAVIEEE! Eaten by this woman of all values ignorant! All the time!"

rows.en: I personified the caviar and mourned his fate.

ghs.assessment: The narrator anthropomorphizes the caviar and pities it. 'I pity that anthropomorphism' instead makes the rhetorical device itself the object of pity.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I anthropomorphize it and mourn its fate.'

highlights.text: I pity that anthropomorphism.

ghs.assessment: 泣かれても means that his crying leaves her at a loss or will not help. 'Crying, really now' is a fragment and does not state her response to being cried at.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Crying won't help...'

highlights.text: Touko: "Crying, really now."

rows.jp: 「だから！　ご自慢のキャビアはどうしたのか訊いたんだ！」
rows.en: “Then answer me! What happened to that precious caviar of yours?!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Therefore! I now ask what happened to this proud caviar!"
ghs.assessment: だから is an emphatic 'I'm asking you,' not the formal connective 'Therefore.' ご自慢 means prized or vaunted, not 'proud,' and the question concerns what happened to it.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I'm asking what happened to your precious caviar!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Therefore! I now ask what happened to this proud caviar!"

rows.jp: 「今週分はないわ。昨日送られてこなかったし」
rows.en: “There isn’t any this week. Nothing came yesterday.”

ghs.en: Touko: "This week there's none, no. It wasn't delivered yesterday."

rows.jp: 「先週は全然食べなくて未開封だったけれど……捨ててしまったわ。傷むもの」
rows.en: “I didn’t eat any last week, so it was still unopened... but I threw it away. It goes bad.”

ghs.en: Touko: "Last week we didn't eat any of it and it was still sealed, but... I threw it all away. It's perishable."
ghs.assessment: Japanese omits the subject. First-person Touko is likeliest, but household we is contextually possible in a staffed rich household.
ghs.remedy: Prefer a subject-neutral or clearly contextual formulation.

highlights.text: Touko: "Last week we didn't eat any of it and it was still sealed, but... I threw it all away. It's perishable."

ghs.assessment: イクッ is the climactic cry 'I'm coming!' used as an exaggerated reaction. 'BNK' substitutes an unexplained impact sound and removes the sexualized joke.
ghs.remedy: Use a controlled equivalent of the climactic cry.

highlights.text: Taichi: "BNK!!!"

rows.en: My whole body snapped into a rigid arch.

ghs.en: I push out my chest and start to bend backwards,
ghs.assessment: ぴーんと反った says the narrator's body snaps into a rigid backward arch. 'Push out my chest and start to bend backwards' adds a deliberate chest action and weakens the sudden full-body motion.
ghs.remedy: Use 'My body snaps backward into an arch.'

highlights.text: I push out my chest and start to bend backwards,

rows.jp: そのまま地面に倒れる。
rows.en: I toppled over onto the ground.

ghs.en: until the back of my head hits the ground.
ghs.assessment: The source says he falls to the ground in that posture. The English adds a specific impact of the back of his head and turns the fall into a gradual endpoint.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Still like that, I fall to the ground.'

highlights.text: until the back of my head hits the ground.

rows.jp: ブリッジを保持したまま、全身を痙攣させる。
rows.en: Still locked in a backbend, I convulsed from head to toe.

ghs.en: While still arcing the back as a bridge, I begin convulsing all throughout.

rows.jp: 「キャビア……捨てた……これから傷むから……傷む前に捨てた……」
rows.en: “Caviar... thrown away... because it was going to spoil... thrown away before it spoiled...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Caviar... thrown away... because it is going to spoil... thrown before it spoiled..."

rows.jp: 「俺が中国株で幼少のみぎりから貯えた全財産を失ったというのに……」
rows.en: “I lost every cent I had saved since childhood on Chinese stocks...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Even though I had lost the entire fortune I had saved up since my days of infancy on Chinese stock..."

rows.jp: 「おまえはキャビアを捨てていたなんて！！」

ghs.en: Taichi: "You have just been throwing caviar away!!!"

rows.jp: 「支離滅裂でもう何がなにやら……」
rows.en: “You’re making so little sense I don’t even know where to start...”

ghs.en: Touko: "What are you doing with all this incoherent and illogical nonsense..."
ghs.assessment: Tōko says his speech is so incoherent that she can no longer tell what is what. 'What are you doing with ... nonsense' changes confusion about meaning into a question about an action.
ghs.remedy: Use 'This is so incoherent I can't even tell what you're talking about anymore...'

highlights.text: Touko: "What are you doing with all this incoherent and illogical nonsense..."

rows.en: “This is the problem with rich people!”

ghs.assessment: だから金持ちは is the exasperated generalization 'That's rich people for you!' 'Why you over-rich' is not grammatical and changes it into a direct accusation of excess wealth.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That's rich people for you!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Why you over-rich...!"

ghs.assessment: The source says Tōko lowers her face. 'Tōko's face looks downcast' makes the face the subject and substitutes an inferred emotion for the physical action.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Tōko lowers her head.'

highlights.text: Touko's face looks downcast.

rows.jp: 「……お金なんて、もう意味ないじゃない」

ghs.en: Touko: "...rich you say, but now it's all meaningless."
ghs.assessment: The source says money no longer has any meaning. 'Rich you say' invents a reply to the prior label and makes wealth, rather than money, the explicit topic.
ghs.remedy: Use '...Money doesn't mean anything anymore.'

highlights.text: Touko: "...rich you say, but now it's all meaningless."

ghs.assessment: そらそーだが concedes once that this is true before qualifying it. 'Sure, suuure' adds dismissive repetition not present in the source.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That's true, but...'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Sure, suuure, but!"

rows.jp: 「黒須は、料理できるからいいよね」
rows.en: “Lucky you, Kurosu. You know how to cook.”

ghs.en: Touko: "Kurosu, you can cook, that's great."

rows.jp: 「料理って言うか、焼いただけだけど」
rows.en: “Calling it cooking is a stretch. I just roasted them.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Cooking, now, it's just roasting something I rustled up."
ghs.assessment: The speaker qualifies the act as merely roasting rather than cooking. 'Now' and 'something I rustled up' are additions, and the opening 'Cooking, now' is not a stable English clause.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Cooking? All I did was roast them.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Cooking, now, it's just roasting something I rustled up."

ghs.en: Should be normal to be capable of it.
ghs.assessment: 普通できるだろう means that anyone should be able to do it. 'Should be normal to be capable of it' is a literal nominal construction that omits the general human subject.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Anyone should be able to do that.'

highlights.text: Should be normal to be capable of it.

rows.jp: さいとうた○をの力添えもあるけど。
rows.en: Though I did have some help from Saitō Ta○o.

ghs.en: Though I have had the help of Saitou Ta**o.

rows.jp: 「……面倒になってくる。ただ生きるために努力しないといけないなんて」
rows.en: “...What a pain. Having to make an effort just to stay alive.”

ghs.en: Touko: "...this has become so annoying. All this big effort needed just to live normally."

rows.jp: この女の家には、家政婦がいる。

ghs.en: This woman's family has a housekeeper.

ghs.assessment: Touko is the correct project romanization. The real defect is the opaque untranslated Ojou-sama and its surrounding grammar.
ghs.remedy: Localize the address and repair the sentence.

highlights.text: That's why Touko's an Ojou-sama.

rows.jp: つまり、自分で何かしなくとも自動的に生きてこられたわけだ。
rows.en: She’d made it this far on autopilot, never having to do anything for herself.

ghs.en: In other words, she was maintained alive automatically even without doing anything herself.
ghs.assessment: The source says she has automatically been able to stay alive without doing anything herself. 'Was maintained alive automatically' is an unnatural passive calque that implies an external maintenance process.
ghs.remedy: Use 'In other words, she has always stayed alive automatically without doing anything herself.'

highlights.text: In other words, she was maintained alive automatically even without doing anything herself.

rows.jp: 「桐原は一人では生きられないのだな」
rows.en: “So you really can’t live on your own, Kirihara.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "So, Kirihara, you can't live alone then."

ghs.assessment: The clipped うるさい is a weakened 'Shut up.' The spelling ''ddap' is not a legible or systematically motivated representation of that interruption.
ghs.remedy: Use '...Shut up.' with controlled weakening if required.

highlights.text: Touko: "...'ddap."

rows.jp: 力ない反論が肯定だった。
rows.en: Her feeble protest only confirmed it.

ghs.en: A feeble refutation that was an affirmation.
ghs.assessment: The source states that her feeble rebuttal amounted to an admission. 'A feeble refutation that was an affirmation' is an unattached noun phrase.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Her feeble rebuttal amounted to an admission.'

highlights.text: A feeble refutation that was an affirmation.

ghs.assessment: 自動的なやつ addresses one automatic person or creature. 'Automatic people' pluralizes the target and produces an unnatural insult.
ghs.remedy: Use 'You automatic creature...'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Damn automatic people..."

rows.en: “...Would it be okay if I lived here?”

ghs.assessment: The source is a hesitant request for permission to live here. 'Me staying here, can't I?' uses a dislocated object-like gerund and malformed question syntax.
ghs.remedy: Use '...Could I stay here?'

highlights.text: Touko: "...me staying here, can't I?"

ghs.en: I could not believe my ears.

rows.jp: 本気で弱ってるな、コイツ。
rows.en: She really was in bad shape.

ghs.assessment: Impaired has an ordinary weakened sense available for 弱ってる. The remaining mismatch is overly clinical register.
ghs.remedy: Use weakened or run-down.

highlights.text: She's seriously impaired, this one.

rows.en: And she’d said it so casually.

ghs.en: She even said it all naturally.

rows.jp: 他に頼る相手もいないのは確かで。
rows.en: Then again, she really didn’t have anyone else to turn to.

ghs.en: Then again, there is certainly no one else she could depend on.
